page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g is a general-purpose server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is limited to a 1 GB network-attached volume, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance type.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier. Geekbench single-core scores are also strong. However, multi-core scaling presents a notable tradeoff; multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang are weak. Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET performance, consistently register in the average tier.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, this server is suited for workloads that benefit from strong single-threaded execution but do not require massive multi-core parallelization. Appropriate use cases include text processing, lightweight web serving, and basic database operations. It is less suited for heavy software compilation or medium-to-large language model inference, where prompt processing performance is poor. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC cores offer a stable, non-burstable resource allocation suitable for predictable, continuous workloads without the premium of high-density memory or GPU hardware.
